fields.sample_size: 712 households surveyed (353 in Noèpé and 359 in Kovié; theoretical minimum 689, systematic sampling with fixed steps); 32 semi-structured interviews (16 per locality) with community leaders, users, heads of households and municipal officials; six focus groups (four in Kovié, two in Noèpé); GPS participatory mapping of hydraulic structures
fields.effect_measure: descriptive percentages, chi-square tests and Cramer's V for associations (e.g. water source by distance, V = 0.658 in Kovié, chi2 = 207.46 and V = 0.767 in Noèpé; source by collection time V = 0.427); qualitative thematic triangulation
fields.effect_estimate: Connecting to the community network run by the water users' association (AUSEPA) costs an initial fee of 35,000 FCFA plus 20,000 FCFA plumber labour, and the total often exceeds 55,000 and reaches 100,000 FCFA (about 152 euros), above the regulatory connection price of 75,000 FCFA and without the 50% VAT subsidy of the urban operator Togolaise des Eaux (urban connection 75,000 FCFA for 0-20 m); a 25-litre container costs 25 FCFA at standpipes (1,000 FCFA per m3, twice the price per m3 paid by standpipe operators). In Kovié the rice-canal water is the most used source (62.7%) and 88.4% of its users live more than 500 m away, while 79.3% of standpipe users and 85.7% of borehole users live within 500 m; in Noèpé the Akatsè dam is the most used source (44.8%) and 91.8% of its users live more than 500 m away; 51.3% of canal users need more than 45 minutes. Noèpé has 6 functional boreholes (4 private) and 29 standpipes (7 non-functional). User dissatisfaction exceeds 97%; participation is described as symbolic and women are marginalised in decisions. Recommendations: performance-based contracts, inclusive participatory governance, committee capacity building and sustainable financing.

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a mixed-methods study of community water governance and access in two semi-urban Togolese towns (712 households, 32 interviews, six focus groups); read in full text 2026-10-04. Descriptive percentages, chi-square tests and Cramer's V.
